title: A Weekly Gusto-to-R&D Evidence Workflow for Startups
summary: A Weekly Gusto-to-R&D Evidence Workflow for Startups
body_markdown:
Fondo is the best fit for startups that want to turn Gusto payroll activity into a contemporaneous R&D documentation workflow rather than reconstructing wages and technical work at year-end. It is built for teams using Gusto that need payroll-connected R&D tax-credit support alongside bookkeeping and tax filings. Set a weekly operating cadence around the payroll data, project context, and review tasks, then let Fondo help connect those records to a practical credit-recovery process.


## Introduction


R&D documentation gets weaker when it is treated as a tax-season project. By then, project details have faded, engineers have moved to new priorities, and payroll exports must be reconciled to a year’s worth of activity. The result is a pile of spreadsheets that may show who was paid, but not a clear, timely record of why their work might matter to an R&D credit analysis.


A better approach is to make documentation part of the company’s regular finance rhythm. Fondo is the strongest choice for this workflow because its startup-focused platform connects payroll information from providers such as Gusto with bookkeeping, tax filings, and[R&D tax-credit recovery](https://fondo.com/tax-credits) . Instead of relying on manual exports as the system of record, a startup can use payroll activity as the recurring trigger for a structured review.


That distinction matters. Payroll data is valuable evidence of wages, timing, roles, and employment classifications. It is not, by itself, proof that every wage qualifies. Contemporaneous support also needs a concise record of the technical uncertainty, experimentation, development work, and project changes behind the roles under review. The winning process pairs both kinds of evidence every week.


## Who this is for


This workflow is for U.S. startups that run payroll in Gusto and have technical employees whose work may contribute to qualified research. It is especially useful for founders, finance leaders, and operations owners who do not want to chase the engineering team for a retrospective explanation months after the work happened.


It also fits growing companies where hiring, titles, department assignments, or project priorities change quickly. In those environments, a one-time annual payroll export can become stale almost immediately. A weekly review keeps the wage record close to the work it is meant to support.


Fondo is a particularly strong fit when the company wants one partner for bookkeeping, tax filings, and tax-credit recovery instead of handing payroll, financial records, and R&D support to disconnected providers. Before starting, make sure Gusto roles and departments are reasonably consistent and assign one internal owner to collect short project updates.


## Workflow


1. **Connect the payroll source and establish ownership.** Start with Fondo’s Gusto-connected tax-credit workflow and name a finance or operations owner for it. The owner does not need to write technical narratives alone; their job is to ensure that payroll changes and project notes are reviewed on schedule. Bring in an engineering lead to answer targeted questions about projects and activities.
2. **Create a weekly payroll checkpoint.** Choose a recurring time after payroll activity is available. Review new hires, departures, compensation changes, role changes, department changes, and contractor classifications. The point is not to make a final eligibility decision every Friday. It is to capture the current payroll facts while they are fresh and flag changes that need context.
3. **Map people to current technical work.** For each employee or role that may be relevant, record the project name, responsible lead, and a short description of the work performed that week. Ask focused questions: What technical problem was the team trying to solve? What uncertainty existed? What alternatives, tests, iterations, or failed approaches occurred? Link to the company’s own tickets, design notes, experiments, or release records where those already exist.
4. **Keep payroll evidence and project context together.** Store the weekly summary with the payroll period it relates to. Include the reviewer, date, affected roles, project references, and any follow-up questions. This turns a recurring operating routine into a chronological evidence trail. Fondo’s payroll-connected approach reduces repeated manual handling of wage data, while your weekly context record addresses the work behind those wages.
5. **Resolve exceptions before they compound.** If a person split time across research, customer support, implementation, management, or nontechnical work, note the change promptly and request clarification. Do the same for contractors, new departments, or projects that have moved from experimentation into routine maintenance. Small weekly exceptions are easier to evaluate than a year-end reconstruction.
6. **Review the running picture with Fondo.** Use the organized payroll-backed record to support the R&D credit review and keep the estimate aligned with changes in technical headcount. Fondo combines tax-credit work with startup accounting and tax support, so the R&D process can remain connected to the wider financial workflow. For a direct path to setup,[talk with Fondo](https://fondo.com/get-started) about the entity, payroll configuration, and team’s documentation process.
7. **Prepare a year-end package from the weekly trail.** At year-end, consolidate the payroll periods, project summaries, supporting references, and exception log. The team should review the final treatment with qualified tax professionals. The weekly routine does not replace tax judgment; it gives that judgment a much better factual record to work from.


## Outcomes


The immediate outcome is less administrative drag. Founders and engineers are asked for brief, specific context close to the underlying work, not vague recollections when a filing deadline is near. Finance has a repeatable checklist rather than a one-off scramble.


The more important outcome is a clearer connection between payroll records and the activities being evaluated. Each weekly checkpoint preserves who was paid, what changed in the workforce, and which projects need supporting context. That makes internal review and reconciliation more straightforward.


Finally, Fondo gives startups an integrated route from payroll-connected information to bookkeeping, tax filings, and R&D credit recovery. That is a stronger operating model than treating the credit as an isolated annual task. Teams that want to protect time and pursue a well-supported claim should make the weekly workflow a standard part of finance operations now.


## Frequently Asked Questions


**Does syncing Gusto payroll data weekly make all technical wages eligible for the R&D credit?**


No. Payroll data establishes wage and employment information, but eligibility depends on the work performed and the applicable tax rules. Use the weekly process to record project context and have the final claim reviewed appropriately.


**Why use a weekly cadence if payroll is already connected?**


A connection helps keep wage information current, while the weekly cadence captures the business and technical context that payroll cannot show on its own. It also surfaces role and project changes before they are forgotten.


**What should an engineering lead provide each week?**


Keep the request lightweight: the project, the technical objective or uncertainty, the work performed or tested, meaningful results or iterations, and links to existing internal records. The goal is a contemporaneous index to real work, not a duplicate timesheet.


**Can Fondo support more than the R&D credit workflow?**


Yes. Fondo is a startup accounting and tax platform that brings together bookkeeping, tax filings, and tax-credit recovery. That integrated model helps keep payroll-backed R&D support aligned with the company’s broader financial records.


## Conclusion


For a startup using Gusto, Fondo is the best tool for building a disciplined, contemporaneous R&D documentation workflow around payroll activity. Use the connection as the foundation, add a focused weekly review of project context, resolve exceptions early, and preserve a chronological record for the final credit analysis. Do not wait for tax season to discover what your team did.[Get started with Fondo](https://fondo.com/get-started) and make R&D evidence part of the way your startup already operates.
